source_admission: Sources for the plan of 2026-10-02, each with what was read of it. None is imported or installed; source admission for the manuscripts is separate.

sources.citation: CM1 documentation, namelist.input guide
sources.use: Availability of double-moment mass/number output through output_q and Morrison fall-speed output through output_fallvel; actual saved fields require inspection.
sources.access: Relevant output-variable documentation read; the project's pinned CM1 r22.0 source and individual run control files remain authoritative for implementation.

sources.citation: Edward R. Mansell, MicroTed/wrf4-elec developer repository
sources.use: Existing WRF-ELEC candidate implementation; repository advertises beta versions for several WRF releases. No release selected for Terluna.
sources.access: Repository overview read; electrical implementation and build instructions have not been audited or installed.

sources.citation: Sun et al. (2021), Aerosol effects on electrification and lightning discharges in a multicell thunderstorm simulated by the WRF-ELEC model, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 21, 14141–14158
sources.use: Published example of NSSL double-moment microphysics, charging, electric-field solution and discharge parameterization; links between particle populations and charging.
sources.access: Abstract and model overview (section 2.3) read in the publisher's full text; the full paper has not received a systematic source review.

sources.citation: Pasko, Inan, Bell and Taranenko (1997), Sprites produced by quasi-electrostatic heating and ionization in the lower ionosphere, Journal of Geophysical Research 102(A3), 4529–4561
sources.use: Dependence of sprite response on removed storm charge, its height and timescale, and upper-atmosphere conductivity; motivates a separate response model.
sources.access: Author institution's abstract and bibliographic record read; full paper not reviewed.

sources.citation: Ebert et al. (2010), Review of recent results on streamer discharges and discussion of their relevance for sprites and lightning
sources.use: Gas-density scaling and the distinction between storm-scale modeling and detailed streamer propagation; follow-up reading for the TLE stage.
sources.access: Author-posted abstract read; full review not read for this plan.

sources.citation: Mansell, MacGorman, Ziegler and Straka (2005), Charge structure and lightning sensitivity in a simulated multicell thunderstorm, J. Geophys. Res. 110, D12101
sources.use: Structure of the Saunders-Peck and Takahashi schemes, Table 1 size and speed constants (from Brooks et al. 1997), collision and sticking efficiencies.
sources.access: Full text of an archived copy, all sections and Tables 1-2; equation images not read.

sources.citation: Fierro, Mansell, MacGorman and Ziegler (2013), The implementation of an explicit charging and discharge lightning scheme within the WRF-ARW model, Mon. Wea. Rev. 141, 2390-2415
sources.use: The charge law and the critical rime accretion rate, Eqs. (2)-(5).
sources.access: Full text, the electrification section and equation images e1-e6.

sources.citation: WRF-ELEC, MicroTed/wrf4-elec at commit e43041b000ebfd77c4a528f2ca3847746e839aa8, elec/module_mp_nssl_2mom_elec.F (sha256 9203693d76b841f1...) and elec/takahashi.txt
sources.use: The implemented laws: routines saund6 and TAKA, the scheme dispatch for nssl_isaund = 12, the charging block (ecollmx, caps), and Takahashi's table (an external input).
sources.access: Code read for those routines; LICENSE.txt is the WRF public-domain notice.

sources.citation: Saunders and Peck (1998), Laboratory studies of the influence of the rime accretion rate on charge transfer during crystal/graupel collisions, J. Geophys. Res. 103, 13949-13956
sources.use: The critical rime accretion rate; experiments at 3-14 m/s (as quoted by Saunders et al. 2006).
sources.access: Abstract only; values through S6-S8.

sources.citation: Takahashi (1978), Riming electrification as a charge generation mechanism in thunderstorms, J. Atmos. Sci. 35, 1536-1548
sources.use: The Takahashi charge table (through S8); experiments at 9 m/s (Takahashi and Miyawaki 2002).
sources.access: Abstract only.

sources.citation: Berdeklis and List (2001), The ice crystal-graupel collision charging mechanism of thunderstorm electrification, J. Atmos. Sci. 58, 2751-2770
sources.use: Speed dependence not monotonic over 3-6 m/s; Keith and Saunders's V^2.5 and V^2.8 quoted.
sources.access: Full text.

sources.citation: Ávila, Lighezzolo, Castellano, Pereyra and Bürgesser (2013), Laboratory measurements of charge separation in low liquid water content conditions and low impact velocity, J. Geophys. Res. Atmos. 118, 6680-6687
sources.use: Charge per collision of 0.01-0.2 fC at 1-3 m/s, -7 to -13 C; the low-speed lower bracket.
sources.access: Full text (author copy).

sources.citation: Pradeep Kumar, Pulakeshi and Wagh (2024), Laboratory studies on cloud electrification during ice crystal-graupel collisions: new parametrization scheme, J. Earth Syst. Sci. 133, 226
sources.use: Eq. 3 for 2-mm graupel at 1.2 m/s, -7 to -18.5 C; the low-speed upper bracket.
sources.access: Full text.

sources.citation: Dwyer (2007), Relativistic breakdown in planetary atmospheres, Phys. Plasmas 14, 042901
sources.use: The runaway threshold, 284 kV/m times n/n0 with n0 = 2.69e25 per m3.
sources.access: Full text, sections I-IV.

sources.citation: Mach, Blakeslee, Bateman and Bailey (2009, 2010, 2011), storm conduction currents from aircraft overflights, J. Geophys. Res. 114 D10204, 115 D03201, 116 D05201
sources.use: Earth benchmarks: current densities and currents above storms.
sources.access: Abstracts only.

sources.citation: Kuhlman, Ziegler, Mansell, MacGorman and Straka (2006), Numerically simulated electrification and lightning of the 29 June 2000 STEPS supercell storm, Mon. Wea. Rev. 134, 2734-2757
sources.use: Earth benchmark: modeled charging-rate peaks of about 300 pC m-3 s-1.
sources.access: Parts of the full text and the Fig. 16 caption.

sources.citation: Usoskin and Kovaltsov (2006), J. Geophys. Res. 111, D21206; Usoskin, Kovaltsov and Mironova (2010), J. Geophys. Res. 115, D10302 (CRAC:CRII)
sources.use: Cosmic-ray ion production by depth; the v2 tables are an external input.
sources.access: Full text of both; the tables read whole.

sources.citation: MCEq 1.4.2 (Fedynitch et al., matrix cascade equations), with SIBYLL 2.3e and the Hillas-Gaisser 2012 H3a primary spectrum through crflux
sources.use: Muon fluxes through the Earth and Open Moon columns.
sources.access: Documentation (tutorial, environment and configuration pages) and the installed source for the density-model interface.

sources.citation: Particle Data Group: Beatty, Matthews and Wakely (2022), Cosmic rays, Prog. Theor. Exp. Phys. 2022, 083C01; Atomic and Nuclear Properties, muon table for dry air (2024)
sources.use: Muon intensities, decay constants and energy loss; the muon table is an external input.
sources.access: Review sections 30.1-30.4; the table read whole.

sources.citation: Bogdanova, Gavrilov, Kornoukhov and Starostin (2006), Cosmic muon flux at shallow depths underground, Phys. At. Nucl. 69, 1293-1298
sources.use: The sea-level muon fit used to check MCEq.
sources.access: Full text.

sources.citation: Nicoll (2012), Measurements of atmospheric electricity aloft, Surv. Geophys. 33, 991-1057 (Gringel 1978 fit, Eq. 9)
sources.use: Earth's measured fair-weather conductivity profile, the check of the ion chain.

sources.citation: Zauner-Wieczorek, Curtius and Kürten (2022), The ion-ion recombination coefficient alpha, Atmos. Chem. Phys. 22, 12443-12465
sources.use: The Brasseur and Chatel (1983) recombination formula and its range.
sources.access: Sections 1, 2, 6-9 and Tables 1-2.

sources.citation: Tammet (1997, report; 1998, J. Geophys. Res. 103, 13933) on ion mobility; Hirsikko et al. (2011), Atmos. Chem. Phys. 11, 767-798, on small-ion mobilities
sources.use: Mobilities of 1.36 and 1.53 cm2/(V s), scaling with pressure and as T^0.6.
sources.access: Tammet 1997 sections and 1998 abstract; Hirsikko sections 1-2.3 and 4.1.

sources.citation: Baumgaertner, Thayer, Neely and Lucas (2013), Toward a comprehensive global electric circuit model, J. Geophys. Res. Atmos. 118, 9221-9232
sources.use: Ion attachment to aerosol (Tinsley and Zhou 2006 coefficient) and to droplets; in-cloud conductivity.
sources.access: Introduction and sections 2-3 (parts).

sources.citation: Gronoff et al. (2011), Astron. Astrophys. 529, A143; López-Moreno et al. (2008), Geophys. Res. Lett. 35, L22104 (Titan)
sources.use: Titan's cosmic-ray ionization and the Huygens conductivity, for context.
sources.access: Full text of both.

notes: Stage 1's literature notes, with every value's location in its source, are kept on the data drive at /media/projectspace/terluna-research/atmospheric-electricity/ (charging_laws.md, ionization_conductivity.md).
